'''Qualtrics, LLC''' is an American [[experience management|experience management]] company, with co-headquarters in [[Seattle, Washington]], and [[Provo, Utah]] The company was founded in 2002 by Scott M. Smith, [[Ryan Smith (businessman)|Ryan Smith]], Jared Smith, and Stuart Orgill.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/venturecapital/2012/05/15/qualtrics-taps-accel-sequoia-for-first-ever-vc-round/|title=Qualtrics Taps Accel, Sequoia For First-Ever VC Round|first=Lizette |last=Chapman|work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=15 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Qualtrics Founders: Brothers Who Stick Together & Build a Million Dollar Business |url=https://www.startupgrind.com/blog/qualtrics-founders-brothers-who-stick-together-build-a-million-dollar-business/ |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=Startup Grind |language=en}}</ref>

Qualtrics offers a cloud-based subscription software platform for what they call ''Experience Management'', which it launched in March 2017 and helps companies collect and analyze feedback from employees, customers and others.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Rogers|first=Bruce|title=Ryan Smith's Qualtrics Capitalizes On The Rise Of The 'Experience Economy'|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/brucerogers/2017/03/02/ryan-smiths-qualtrics-capitalizes-on-the-rise-of-the-experience-economy/|access-date=2020-12-28|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref> Qualtrics software is used widely in academia to conduct [[survey research]];<ref>{{Cite web |last=David F Carr |date=24 July 2013 |title="Qualtrics Dominates Academic Survey Research" |url=https://www.informationweek.com/it-leadership/qualtrics-dominates-academic-survey-research |website=[[InformationWeek]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite conference| publisher = ACM| doi = 10.1145/3613904.3642572| isbn = 979-8-4007-0330-0| conference = CHI '24: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems| pages = 1–22| last1 = Velykoivanenko| first1 = Lev| last2 = Salehzadeh Niksirat| first2 = Kavous| last3 = Teofanovic| first3 = Stefan| last4 = Chapuis| first4 = Bertil| last5 = Mazurek| first5 = Michelle L.| last6 = Huguenin| first6 = Kévin| title = Designing a Data-Driven Survey System: Leveraging Participants' Online Data to Personalize Surveys| book-title = Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems| location = Honolulu HI USA| date = 2024-05-11| doi-access = free}}</ref> however, in 2012 the company began to pivot toward serving enterprise customers.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-07-01 |title=The Founder of Qualtrics on Reinventing an Already Successful Business |url=https://hbr.org/2021/07/the-founder-of-qualtrics-on-reinventing-an-already-successful-business |access-date=2025-02-08 |work=Harvard Business Review |language=en |issn=0017-8012}}</ref> As of 2026, the company is focused on data collection and the use of agentic AI.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Preez |first=Derek du |date=2026-03-18 |title=Qualtrics X4 - new CEO Jason Maynard declares the insight gap closed, and sets sights on driving outcomes |url=https://diginomica.com/qualtrics-x4-new-ceo-jason-maynard-declares-insight-gap-closed-and-sets-sights-driving-outcomes |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=diginomica.com |language=en}}</ref>

==History==
Qualtrics was founded in Provo, Utah in 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Feinauer |first=Courtney M. |title=’Trics of the Trade |url=https://magazine.byu.edu/article/trics-of-the-trade/ |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=Y Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> The company began in the Smiths' basement and operated from there for five years. Stuart Orgill, a friend of Ryan Smith, later joined them as the company began to grow.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Feinauer |first=Courtney M. |title=’Trics of the Trade |url=https://magazine.byu.edu/article/trics-of-the-trade/ |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=Y Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

In the company's first decade of operation, more than 1,300 universities used its Qualtrics Research Suite. Its customers also included Boeing, FedEx, and Microsoft.<ref name=":5" />

===2010–2019===
In 2012, the company received a $70{{nbsp}}million [[Series A investment]] from [[Sequoia Capital]] and [[Accel (venture capital firm)|Accel]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbinsights.com/research/venture-capital-peer-rankings/|title=Venture Capital Power Rankings: VCs Rate VCs|date=7 April 2016|website=CB Insights Research|access-date=17 June 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2011/05/25/top-10-vc-firms-investorrank/|title=The Top 10 VC Firms, According To InvestorRank|date=25 May 2011|access-date=17 June 2019}}</ref> It was the largest joint investment to date by these two firms.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2012/05/15/qualtrics-raises-70m-accel-sequoia/|title=Qualtrics Raises $70M From Accel And Sequoia: "The Biggest Software Company You Haven't Heard Of"?|author=Anthony Ha|publisher=AOL|work=TechCrunch|date=15 May 2012 }}</ref> In September 2014, the two firms returned to [[Series B funding]], led by [[Insight Partners]]. The funding, worth $150{{nbsp}}million, was a record for a Utah-based company, and it valued the company at $1{{nbsp}}billion.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.businessweek.com/articles/2014-09-24/how-qualtrics-turned-online-surveys-into-a-1-billion-business|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140925032456/http://www.businessweek.com/articles/2014-09-24/how-qualtrics-turned-online-surveys-into-a-1-billion-business|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 25, 2014|title=How Qualtrics Turned Online Surveys Into a $1{{nbsp}}Billion Business - Businessweek|author=Joshua Brustein|work=Businessweek.com|date=24 September 2014}}</ref>

In May 2016, Qualtrics acquired statistical analysis startup Statwing for an undisclosed sum. Statwing was a San Francisco-based company that created point-and-click software for advanced statistical analysis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mrweb.com/drno/news22721.htm|title=Daily Research News Online no. 22721 - Qualtrics Buys Software Firm Statwing|website=www.mrweb.com|access-date=2016-06-29}}</ref>

In April 2018, the firm acquired Delighted for an undisclosed sum. Delighted had more than 1,500 customers at the time of acquisition.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexkonrad/2018/04/12/qualtrics-acquires-delighted/#4096aec927a2|title=Qualtrics Inches Closer To IPO By Acquiring The Startup Behind Ratings For Postmates And Uber|website=www.forbes.com|access-date=2018-04-12}}</ref>

On October 19, 2018, Qualtrics filed its S-1 registration statement through an initial public offering (IPO).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1747748/000162828018012674/qualtricss-1.htm|title=Qualtrics International Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement Under the Securities Act of 1933|date=October 19, 2018|website=U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission}}</ref> At the time, the company listed over 9,000 global customers.

Plans for the IPO were scrapped when it was announced in November 2018 that Qualtrics would be acquired by [[SAP SE|SAP]] (NYSE: SAP).<ref name=":6">{{Cite news |last=Konrad |first=Alex |title=SAP Plans To Spin Out Qualtrics, Its $8 Billion Acquisition From 2018, For An IPO |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexkonrad/2020/07/26/sap-plans-to-spin-out-qualtrics-for-ipo/ |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20251006221959/https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexkonrad/2020/07/26/sap-plans-to-spin-out-qualtrics-for-ipo/ |archive-date=2025-10-06 |access-date=2026-09-02 |work=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

SAP bought Qualtrics in January 2019 for US$8{{nbsp}}billion in an all-cash deal.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Shu |first=Catherine |date=2018-11-12 |title=SAP agrees to buy Qualtrics for $8B in cash, just before the survey software company's IPO |url=https://techcrunch.com/2018/11/11/sap-agrees-to-buy-qualtrics-for-8b-in-cash-just-before-the-survey-software-companys-ipo/ |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.sap.com/2019/01/sap-completes-qualtrics-acquisition/|title=SAP Completes Qualtrics Acquisition|date=2019-01-23|website=SAP News Center|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-04|archive-date=2022-02-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220219043751/https://news.sap.com/2019/01/sap-completes-qualtrics-acquisition/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Qualtrics Acquisition: Two Essential Actions Customers Should Take |url=https://www.npifinancial.com/blog/qualtrics-acquisition-two-essential-actions-customers-should-take |access-date=20 January 2026 |website=NPI Financial}}</ref>

=== 2020–present ===
On July 26, 2020, SAP announced its intent to take Qualtrics public through an IPO in the United States.<ref name=":6" /> According to SAP, the decision to go public was made due to Qualtrics' performance since the acquisition, with 2019 cloud growth in excess of 40 percent.<ref name=":7">{{Cite news |date=2020-07-27 |title=SAP To Spin Off Qualtrics Unit |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/sap-to-spin-off-qualtrics-unit-11595826277 |access-date=2026-09-02 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> SAP's stated intent was to remain the majority owner of Qualtrics, while Qualtrics co-founder Ryan Smith remained the company's largest shareholder.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lev-Ram |first=Michal |title=SAP says goodbye to Qualtrics, less than two years after buying it for $8 billion |url=https://fortune.com/2020/07/26/sap-qualtrics-public-offering/ |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=Fortune |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":7" />

On January 28, 2021, Qualtrics began trading on the Nasdaq at $41.85 per share.<ref name="CNBC_IPO">{{cite web |last1=Bursztynsky |first1=Jessica |last2=Levy |first2=Ari |title=Qualtrics closes up 51% after debut, valuing cloud software vendor at $27.3{{nbsp}}billion |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/28/qualtrics-ipo-xm-begins-trading-on-the-nasdaq.html |website=CNBC |access-date=28 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128231038/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/28/qualtrics-ipo-xm-begins-trading-on-the-nasdaq.html |archive-date=28 January 2021 |language=en |date=28 January 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> 

In January 2021, Brad Anderson, a high level executive of Microsoft, joined Qualtrics as president of products and services.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Corporate Vice President Brad Anderson is leaving Microsoft for Qualtrics |url=https://www.zdnet.com/home-and-office/work-life/corporate-vice-president-brad-anderson-is-leaving-microsoft-for-qualtrics/ |access-date=2025-09-25 |website=ZDNET |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kuhlman |first=Cara |date=2021-01-22 |title=Tech Moves: Microsoft's Brad Anderson jumps to Qualtrics in wave of pre-IPO hires; Elena Donio joins Databricks board; Hiya, Esper add startup vets |url=https://www.geekwire.com/2021/tech-moves-microsofts-brad-anderson-jumps-qualtrics-wave-pre-ipo-hires-elena-donio-joins-databricks-board-hiya-esper-add-startup-vets/ |access-date=2025-09-25 |website=GeekWire |language=en-US}}</ref>

In October 2021, the firm acquired Clarabridge in an all-stock deal for $1.125{{nbsp}}billion. Clarabridge was a Virginia-based company that created software for omnichannel conversational analytics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forrester.com/blogs/qualtricss-1-125b-acquisition-of-clarabridge-upends-the-customer-feedback-management-market|title=Qualtrics' $1.125B Acquisition Of Clarabridge Upends The Customer Feedback Management Market|date=30 July 2021 |access-date=2021-07-30}}</ref>

In May 2022, Qualtrics announced it would go live on Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud infrastructure in London in the second half of 2022. Qualtrics customers would be able to access the XM Platform locally via AWS London region. Furthermore, Qualtrics announced it would be opening a London office and customer experience centre.<ref>{{cite journal|date=12 May 2022|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20220512005097/en/Qualtrics-to-go-live-on-Amazon-Web-Services-Cloud-Infrastructure-in-the-UK|title=Qualtrics UK customers will be able to access the Qualtrics XM/OS platform locally via data centre in the AWS London Region|journal=Business Wire|access-date=12 May 2022}}</ref>

In March 2023, a group of investors including private equity firm [[Silver Lake (investment firm)|Silver Lake]], [[CPP Investment Board]], and co-founder [[Ryan Smith (businessman)|Ryan Smith]] agreed to buy Qualtrics from SAP in an all-cash deal worth $12.5{{nbsp}}billion.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gara |first=Antoine |date=13 March 2023 |title=Silver Lake set to take over software company Qualtrics in $12.5bn deal |url=https://www.ft.com/content/fae1f119-2d45-4285-8b9d-0f119937578f |newspaper=[[Financial Times]] |url-access=limited}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Capoot |first=Ashley |date=2023-03-13 |title=Silver Lake and CPP Investments to acquire Qualtrics for $12.5{{nbsp}}billion |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2023/03/13/silver-lake-and-cpp-investments-to-acquire-qualtrics-for-12point5-billion.html |access-date=2026-01-23 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref>

Silver Lake first invested more than $500{{nbsp}}million in Qualtrics during the company's IPO in 2021.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.silverlake.com/portfolio/qualtrics/ | title=Qualtrics |website=Silver Lake.com }}</ref> In March 2023, Silver Lake agreed to take Qualtrics private. In June 2023, the Qualtrics acquisition by Silver Lake was completed. At the time of the close, the Qualtrics deal was the single largest investment in Silver Lake's history.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Qualtrics acquired by Silver Lake for $12.5bn |url=https://www.financierworldwide.com/qualtrics-acquired-by-silver-lake-for-125bn |access-date=2025-09-25 |website=Financier Worldwide |language=en-US}}</ref>

In connection with the close, Accel, a global venture capital firm, as well as [[BDT & MSD Partners]], a merchant bank built to serve the distinct needs of business owners and strategic, long-term investors; and [[DFO Management]], the family investment office of Michael Dell, joined Silver Lake in investing in Qualtrics. Accel, which was one of Qualtrics' earliest investors, invested $500{{nbsp}}million. BDT & MSD Partners and DFO Management each made a co-investment of $250{{nbsp}}million, for an aggregate commitment of $500{{nbsp}}million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-29 |title=Silver Lake and CPP Investments complete $12.5bn Qualtrics acquisition |url=https://www.privateequitywire.co.uk/silver-lake-and-cpp-investments-complete-125bn-qualtrics-acquisition/ |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=Private Equity Wire |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In August 2025, Qualtrics and PureSpectrum entered into a partnership aimed at accelerating research teams' access to market insights related to synthetic research capabilities. Through the agreement, PureSpectrum designated Qualtrics as its exclusive synthetic panel provider.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Watson |first=Melania |date=2025-08-05 |title=Qualtrics & PureSpectrum partner to speed up synthetic research |url=https://channellife.news/story/qualtrics-purespectrum-partner-to-speed-up-synthetic-research |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=ChannelLife US |language=en}}</ref>

In October 2025, Qualtrics announced the acquisition of Indiana-based healthcare-focused technology company [[Press Ganey]] for $6.75{{nbsp}}billion, including debt, making it the company's largest acquisition to date.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Gara |first1=Antoine |last2=Barnes |first2=Oliver |date=October 5, 2025 |title=Software group Qualtrics to buy health-tech company Press Ganey Forsta for $6.7bn |url=https://www.ft.com/content/44c9959f-a3e2-41a6-941b-c4ddaf731067 |work=Financial Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Soper |first=Taylor |date=2025-10-07 |title=Qualtrics to acquire healthcare data giant Press Ganey Forsta in $6.75B deal |url=https://www.geekwire.com/2025/qualtrics-to-acquire-healthcare-data-giant-press-ganey-forsta-in-6-75b-deal/ |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=GeekWire |language=en-US}}</ref> The acquisition, which was finalized in May 2026, expanded Qualtrics’ healthcare network to include 41,000 facilities using Press Ganey Forsta systems.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fox |first=Andrea |date=2026-05-20 |title=Qualtrics eyes a data engine to predict the experiences patients want |url=https://www.healthcareitnews.com/news/qualtrics-eyes-data-engine-predict-experiences-patients-want |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=www.healthcareitnews.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-19 |title=After a debt deal hiccup in March, Qualtrics finally completes $US6.75bn acquisition of Press Ganey Forsta |url=http://www.mi-3.com.au/19-05-2026/after-debt-deal-hiccup-march-qualtrics-finally-completes-us675bn-acquisition-press-ganey |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=www.mi-3.com.au |language=en}}</ref> Qualtrics' acquisition of Press Ganey Forsta was reportedly the largest technology acquisition in Utah history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-19 |title=Qualtrics Completes US$7 Billion Acquisition Of Press Ganey Forsta In Healthcare Experience Play |url=https://smbtech.au/blog/qualtrics-completes-us7-billion-acquisition-of-press-ganey-forsta-in-healthcare-experience-play/ |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=smbtech.au}}</ref>

On February 3, 2026, Qualtrics named Jason Maynard its new CEO and appointed Maynard to its board of directors.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Doerer |first=Kristen |date=2026-02-03 |title=Qualtrics appoints former Oracle executive CEO |url=https://www.customerexperiencedive.com/news/qualtrics-appoints-jason-maynard-ceo/811267/ |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=www.customerexperiencedive.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Carmona |first=Aliza |date=2026-02-04 |title=Jason Maynard appointed CEO of Qualtrics, joins Board of Directors |url=https://marketech-apac.com/jason-maynard-appointed-ceo-of-qualtrics-joins-board-of-directors/ |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=MARKETECH APAC |language=en-US}}</ref> Maynard, the former executive vice president of revenue operations at Oracle, replaced Jim Whitehurst and Mark Gillett, who became interim co-CEOs after Zig Serafin stepped down as CEO in October 2025.<ref name=":4" />

In March 2026, the PGA Tour named Qualtrics the official tool of its new "Voice of the Gallery" program, part of the Tour's Fan Forward initiative.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=PGA TOUR, Qualtrics announce expanded relationship to enhance fan experiences |url=https://www.pgatour.com/article/news/company/2026/03/18/pga-tour-qualtrics-announce-expanded-relationship-to-enhance-fan-experiences |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=www.pgatour.com |language=en}}</ref>

At Qualtrics' X4 Experience Management Summit in March 2026, the company introduced new artificial intelligence capabilities, including synthetic consumer panels that allow organizations to simulate how consumers may respond to research questions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gillin |first=Paul |date=2026-03-18 |title=Qualtrics adds AI-powered synthetic data and research tools to speed customer insights |url=https://siliconangle.com/2026/03/18/qualtrics-adds-ai-powered-synthetic-data-research-tools-speed-customer-insights/ |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=SiliconANGLE |language=en-US}}</ref> The panels were tested by Google, Navy Federal Credit Union, and Dollar Shave Club, among other companies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fluckinger |first=Don |date=2026-03-18 |title=Qualtrics expands synthetic research marketing, testing tech |url=https://www.techtarget.com/enterprise-software/news/366640444/Qualtrics-expands-synthetic-research-marketing-testing-tech |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=Enterprise Software |language=en}}</ref>
